gates.description: Canonical identity/evidence and existing runtime/debug/replay regression oracles remain green.
Runtime module bindings, generations, ASLR resolution, and cross-version identity gates fail closed.
One provider owns one canonical runtime session with explicit facets and compatibility adapters.
RuntimeEvent ordering, dedupe, epoch, loss, and completeness contracts remain conservative.
Runtime evidence attaches only through validated identity and mutations retain intervention ancestry.
Trace import/replay is immutable, deterministic about known data, bounded, and identity-safe.
Provider protocol negotiation is additive to debugger v1 and enforces namespace/version/epoch/cancellation boundaries.
Debugger providers share lifecycle, module generation, event, cancellation, and intervention semantics.
Instrumentation is first-class; observation and mutation are separated and mutation authority is provider-owned.
Emulator providers are backend-neutral and emit explicitly synthetic, bounded runtime evidence.
Cross-version runtime/static attachment requires explicit strong match evidence.
Partial, unsupported, dropped, or truncated runtime data can never be upgraded by aggregation.
Debugger, Instrumentation, Trace, and Emulator compose through one provider plane and canonical evidence system.
The living integration diff remains inside the declared Phase 10 ownership envelope.
